ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الر تِلْكَ آيَاتُ الْكِتَابِ الْحَكِيمِ (١)).
The discussion of the disjointed letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿa) has preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara and al-Aʿrāf, and the rest are judged by analogy with those two. And (الْحَكِيمِ) is in the sense of الْمُحْكَمِ ("made firm, precise"). It is also said: it is in the sense of الْحَاكِمِ ("the one who judges").

ukberi-tibyan:2-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَكَانَ لِلنَّاسِ عَجَبًا أَنْ أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى رَجُلٍ مِنْهُمْ أَنْ أَنْذِرِ النَّاسَ وَبَشِّرِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنَّ لَهُمْ قَدَمَ صِدْقٍ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ قَالَ الْكَافِرُونَ إِنَّ هَذَا لَسَاحِرٌ مُبِينٌ (٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَكَانَ لِلنَّاسِ عَجَبًا أَنْ أَوْحَيْنَا): it is the ism (subject) of kāna, and its khabar (predicate) is عَجَبًا. And (لِلنَّاسِ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from عَجَبٍ, because the implied form is "was it a wonder to the people". It is also said: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to كَانَ. It is also said: it is attached to عَجَبٍ by way of clarification (tabyīn). It is also said: (عَجَبٌ) here is in the sense of مُعْجِبٌ ("astonishing"); and when a maṣdar (verbal noun) occurs in the place of a passive or active participle, what it governs may precede it, as with the passive participle.
(أَنْ أَنْذِرِ النَّاسَ): أَنْ may be maṣdariyya (forming a maṣdar), its position then being accusative by أَوْحَيْنَا; or it may be in the sense of أَيْ ("that is"), in which case it has no position.

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ اسْتَوَى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ يُدَبِّرُ الْأَمْرَ مَا مِنْ شَفِيعٍ إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ إِذْنِهِ ذَلِكُمُ اللَّهُ رَبُّكُمْ فَاعْبُدُوهُ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ (٣))
His saying, Exalted is He: (يُدَبِّرُ الْأَمْرَ): it may be resumptive, or a second khabar (predicate), or a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِلَيْهِ مَرْجِعُكُمْ جَمِيعًا وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقًّا إِنَّهُ يَبْدَأُ الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ لِيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ بِالْقِسْطِ وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَهُمْ شَرَابٌ مِنْ حَمِيمٍ وَعَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْفُرُونَ (٤))
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَعْدَ اللَّهِ): it is accusative (manṣūb) as a maṣdar (verbal noun) by a verb indicated by the speech, namely His saying (إِلَيْهِ مَرْجِعُكُمْ); because this is a promise from Him, Glorified is He, of the resurrection.
And (حَقًّا) is another maṣdar, its implied form being "that has been made true, truly".
(إِنَّهُ يَبْدَأُ): the majority read it with kasra on the hamza, as a new beginning (istiʾnāf). It has also been read with fatḥa on it, the implied form being "it is true that He begins", so it is the fāʿil (agent). The implied form may also be "because He begins". The past tense of يَبْدَأُ is بَدَأَ, and there is another dialectal form of it: أَبْدَأَ. (بِمَا كَانُوا): in the position of the nominative, as another naʿt (adjective) of عَذَابٌ; and it may be the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject).

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ ضِيَاءً وَالْقَمَرَ نُورًا وَقَدَّرَهُ مَنَازِلَ لِتَعْلَمُوا عَدَدَ السِّنِينَ وَالْحِسَابَ مَا خَلَقَ اللَّهُ ذَلِكَ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ يُفَصِّلُ الْآيَاتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ (٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (جَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ ضِيَاءً): two objects. It is also possible that (ضِيَاءً) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), with جَعَلَ in the sense of خَلَقَ ("created"), the implied form being "possessing light".
It is also said: the sun is itself the light. The yāʾ is changed from a wāw, as you say ضَوْءٌ, and the hamza is a radical. It is also read with two hamzas with an alif between them. The explanation of this is that the yāʾ was moved back and the hamza moved forward; then when the yāʾ fell at the end after an extra alif, it was changed to hamza according to some, and according to others to alif, after which the alif was changed to hamza so that two alifs would not come together. (وَالْقَمَرَ نُورًا): i.e. "possessing light". It is also said: the maṣdar (verbal noun) is in the sense of the active participle, i.e. "illuminating". (وَقَدَّرَهُ مَنَازِلَ): i.e. "and He determined for it", the preposition being omitted. It is also said: the implied form is "He determined it as possessing stations"; on this view «وَقَدَّرَ» is transitive to two objects, because its meaning is "made" and "rendered".
It is also possible that قَدَّرَ is transitive to one object, in the sense of "created", and مَنَازِلَ is a ḥāl, i.e. "moving from one station to another".

ukberi-tibyan:7-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ لَا يَرْجُونَ لِقَاءَنَا وَرَضُوا بِالْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَاطْمَأَنُّوا بِهَا وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ عَنْ آيَاتِنَا غَافِلُونَ (٧) أُولَئِكَ مَأْوَاهُمُ النَّارُ بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ (٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ لَا يَرْجُونَ): the khabar (predicate) of inna is (أُولَئِكَ مَأْوَاهُمُ النَّارُ). أُولَئِكَ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), مَأْوَاهُمْ is a second mubtadaʾ, النَّارُ is its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of أُولَئِكَ. (بِمَا كَانُوا): the bāʾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted verb indicated by the speech; i.e. "they were requited for what they used to earn".

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ يَهْدِيهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ بِإِيمَانِهِمْ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهِمُ الْأَنْهَارُ فِي جَنَّاتِ النَّعِيمِ (٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهِمُ): it may be resumptive, or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object pronoun in يَهْدِيهِمْ; the meaning then is: "He guides them in Paradise to what they desire, in this state".
(فِي جَنَّاتِ): it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to تَجْرِي; or be a ḥāl from الْأَنْهَارُ; or be attached to يَهْدِي; or be a ḥāl from the object pronoun in يَهْدِي; or be a second khabar (predicate) of inna.

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (دَعْوَاهُمْ فِيهَا سُبْحَانَكَ اللَّهُمَّ وَتَحِيَّتُهُمْ فِيهَا سَلَامٌ وَآخِرُ دَعْوَاهُمْ أَنِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ (١٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (دَعْوَاهُمْ): a mubtadaʾ (subject). (سُبْحَانَكَ): accusative (manṣūb) as a maṣdar (verbal noun), and it is the explanation of the "call" (al-daʿwā), because the meaning is: "their saying is سُبْحَانَكَ اللَّهُمَّ". And (فِيهَا) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to تَحِيَّةٌ. (أَنِ الْحَمْدُ): أَنْ is lightened from the heavy (form).
It is also read «أَنَّ» with a doubled nūn, and it is maṣdariyya (forming a maṣdar); the implied form is: "the last of their call is the praise of Allah".

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَوْ يُعَجِّلُ اللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ الشَّرَّ اسْتِعْجَالَهُمْ بِالْخَيْرِ لَقُضِيَ إِلَيْهِمْ أَجَلُهُمْ فَنَذَرُ الَّذِينَ لَا يَرْجُونَ لِقَاءَنَا فِي طُغْيَانِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ (١١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الشَّرَّ): it is the object of يُعَجِّلُ.
And (اسْتِعْجَالَهُمْ): its implied form is "a hastening like their seeking to hasten"; so the maṣdar (verbal noun) and its naʿt (adjective), which was in a genitive construct, were omitted, and the muḍāf ilayhi was put in their place.
Some of them said: it is accusative on the assumption that the preposition is omitted, i.e. "like their seeking to hasten" (ka-stiʿjālihim). This is far-fetched, since if that were permissible, زَيْدٌ غُلَامَ عَمْرٍو ("Zayd is ʿAmr's servant") would be permissible; and on this basis a group judged it weak. But that is not a sound grounds for weakening it, since in the example mentioned there is no verb that becomes transitive by itself when the preposition is dropped, whereas in the āya there is a verb for which that is valid, namely His saying «يُعَجِّلُ».
(فَنَذَرُ): it is conjoined to an omitted verb, its implied form being: "but We grant them respite, and so We leave …". It cannot be conjoined to (يُعَجِّلُ), since if it were so it would be included in the impossibility that (لَوْ) entails; and that is not the case, because the hastening did not happen, whereas their being left in their transgression did happen.

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا مَسَّ الْإِنْسَانَ الضُّرُّ دَعَانَا لِجَنْبِهِ أَوْ قَاعِدًا أَوْ قَائِمًا فَلَمَّا كَشَفْنَا عَنْهُ ضُرَّهُ مَرَّ كَأَنْ لَمْ يَدْعُنَا إِلَى ضُرٍّ مَسَّهُ كَذَلِكَ زُيِّنَ لِلْمُسْرِفِينَ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ (١٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِجَنْبِهِ): in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial); i.e. "he calls upon Us lying down". Likewise (قَاعِدًا أَوْ قَائِمًا). It is also said: what governs these ḥāls is مَسَّ; but that is weak for two reasons. First: on this view the ḥāl would occur after the answer of إِذَا, and that is not the proper way.
Second: the meaning is the frequency of his supplication in all his states, not that harm afflicts him in all his states; and many verses in the Qurʾan have come in accordance with this.
(كَأَنْ لَمْ يَدْعُنَا): in the position of the ḥāl from the agent in «مَرَّ».
(إِلَى ضُرٍّ): i.e. "to the removal of a harm". The lām in لِجَنْبِهِ keeps its original meaning according to the Basrans, and the implied form is "he calls upon Us, laying himself on his side".

ukberi-tibyan:13-13.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ أَهْلَكْنَا الْقُرُونَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ لَمَّا ظَلَمُوا وَجَاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ وَمَا كَانُوا لِيُؤْمِنُوا كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي الْقَوْمَ الْمُجْرِمِينَ (١٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to أَهْلَكْنَا, and it is not a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْقُرُونَ, because it is time.
And (وَجَاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ): it may be a ḥāl, i.e. "when their messengers had come to them"; and it may be conjoined to ظَلَمُوا.

ukberi-tibyan:14-14.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَاكُمْ خَلَائِفَ فِي الْأَرْضِ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ لِنَنْظُرَ كَيْفَ تَعْمَلُونَ (١٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِنَنْظُرَ): it is read, among the irregular (shādhdh) readings, with a single nūn and a doubled ẓāʾ; its explanation is that the second nūn was changed to ẓāʾ and assimilated.

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ لَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ مَا تَلَوْتُهُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَا أَدْرَاكُمْ بِهِ فَقَدْ لَبِثْتُ فِيكُمْ عُمُرًا مِنْ قَبْلِهِ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ (١٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَا أَدْرَاكُمْ بِهِ): it is a past verb, from دَرَيْتَ ("you knew"); the implied sense is: "had Allah willed, He would not have made you know the Qurʾan". It is also read وَلَأَدْرَاكُمْ بِهِ as an affirmation; the meaning is: "and had Allah willed, He would have made you know it without an intermediary".
And it is read among the irregular (shādhdh) readings «وَلَا أَدْرَأَكُمْ بِهِ», with a hamza in place of the alif. It is said: this is a dialect of some Arabs, who change an alif that replaces a yāʾ into a hamza. It is also said: it is an error, because its reader thought it was from al-darʾ, which is "repelling". It is also said: it is not an error, and the meaning is: "had Allah willed, He would have repelled you from believing in it".
(عُمُرًا): it is accusative in the manner of adverbs (ẓurūf); i.e. "the extent of a lifetime" or "the duration of a lifetime".

ukberi-tibyan:18-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مَا لَا يَضُرُّهُمْ وَلَا يَنْفَعُهُمْ وَيَقُولُونَ هَؤُلَاءِ شُفَعَاؤُنَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ قُلْ أَتُنَبِّئُونَ اللَّهَ بِمَا لَا يَعْلَمُ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَلَا فِي الْأَرْضِ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ (١٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا لَا يَضُرُّهُمْ): (مَا) is in the sense of الَّذِي ("that which"), and the idols are meant by it; for this reason He, Exalted is He, said «هَؤُلَاءِ شُفَعَاؤُنَا», using the plural in accordance with the meaning of (مَا).

ukberi-tibyan:21-21.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا أَذَقْنَا النَّاسَ رَحْمَةً مِنْ بَعْدِ ضَرَّاءَ مَسَّتْهُمْ إِذَا لَهُمْ مَكْرٌ فِي آيَاتِنَا قُلِ اللَّهُ أَسْرَعُ مَكْرًا إِنَّ رُسُلَنَا يَكْتُبُونَ مَا تَمْكُرُونَ (٢١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِذَا أَذَقْنَا): the answer of the first (إِذَا) is the second (إِذَا). The second is for surprise (mufājaʾa), and what governs the second is the settledness (istiqrār) contained in (لَهُمْ). It is also said: the second «إِذَا» is temporal as well; and the second together with what follows it is the answer of the first.

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هُوَ الَّذِي يُسَيِّرُكُمْ فِي الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ حَتَّى إِذَا كُنْتُمْ فِي الْفُلْكِ وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِمْ بِرِيحٍ طَيِّبَةٍ وَفَرِحُوا بِهَا جَاءَتْهَا رِيحٌ عَاصِفٌ وَجَاءَهُمُ الْمَوْجُ مِنْ كُلِ مَكَانٍ وَظَنُّوا أَنَّهُمْ أُحِيطَ بِهِمْ دَعَوُا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ لَئِنْ أَنْجَيْتَنَا مِنْ هَذِهِ لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الشَّاكِرِينَ (٢٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يُسَيِّرُكُمْ): it is read with sīn, from al-sayr ("travelling"); and (يَنْشُرُكُمْ), from al-nashr ("spreading"); i.e. "He moves you about and disperses you". (وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِمْ): the pronoun of the absent third person; it is a turn from address to the third person (iltifāt). Had He said «بِكُمْ», it would have matched كُنْتُمْ; and likewise «فَرِحُوا» and what follows it. (جَاءَتْهَا): the pronoun refers to the ships (al-fulk). It is also said: to the wind.

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَمَّا أَنْجَاهُمْ إِذَا هُمْ يَبْغُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنَّمَا بَغْيُكُمْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ مَتَاعَ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا ثُمَّ إِلَيْنَا مَرْجِعُكُمْ فَنُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ (٢٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذَا هُمْ): it is the answer of (لَمَّا), and it is the إِذَا of surprise (mufājaʾa), like the one with which a condition is answered. (بَغْيُكُمْ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject). Regarding the khabar (predicate) there are two views. First: «عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ», with عَلَى attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, i.e. "existing (kāʾin)", not to the maṣdar (verbal noun), because the khabar is not attached to the mubtadaʾ. On this view «مَتَاعُ» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is an enjoyment", or a khabar after a khabar. Second: that the khabar is مَتَاعٌ, and عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ is attached to the maṣdar. And «مَتَاعَ» is read in the accusative; on this view «عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ» is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and «مَتَاعَ» is accusative as a maṣdar, i.e. "He gave you enjoyment of that, an enjoyment". It is also said: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), governed by بَغْيُكُمْ, al-baghy here being in the sense of "seeking"; i.e. "your seeking, against yourselves, the enjoyment of the life of this world". On this view «عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ» is not the khabar, because a maṣdar does not govern what comes after its khabar; rather «عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ» is attached to the maṣdar, and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being: "your seeking the enjoyment of the life of this world is misguidance", or the like.
And مَتَاعِ is read in the genitive, as a naʿt (adjective) of الْأَنْفُسِ, the implied form being "possessing enjoyment".
The maṣdar may also be in the sense of the active participle, i.e. "those that enjoy this world (mumattiʿāt al-dunyā)". It is weak for it to be a badal (substitute), since it is possible to make it a naʿt.

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّمَا مَثَلُ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا كَمَاءٍ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ فَاخْتَلَطَ بِهِ نَبَاتُ الْأَرْضِ مِمَّا يَأْكُلُ النَّاسُ وَالْأَنْعَامُ حَتَّى إِذَا أَخَذَتِ الْأَرْضُ زُخْرُفَهَا وَازَّيَّنَتْ وَظَنَّ أَهْلُهَا أَنَّهُمْ قَادِرُونَ عَلَيْهَا أَتَاهَا أَمْرُنَا لَيْلًا أَوْ نَهَارًا فَجَعَلْنَاهَا حَصِيدًا كَأَنْ لَمْ تَغْنَ بِالْأَمْسِ كَذَلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ الْآيَاتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ (٢٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَاخْتَلَطَ بِهِ نَبَاتُ الْأَرْضِ): the bāʾ is causal; i.e. "the vegetation intermingled because of the water's reaching it". It is also said: the meaning is "the vegetation of the earth mixed with it", i.e. it joined it and so nourished it. And «مِمَّا يَأْكُلُ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from النَّبَاتُ. (وَازَّيَّنَتْ): its origin is تَزَيَّنَتْ; then what we mentioned at (فَادَّارَأْتُمْ فِيهَا) was applied to it.
It is also read with fatḥa on the hamza, sukūn on the zāy, and a yāʾ with fatḥa after it, with the nūn and the yāʾ light (undoubled); i.e. "it became possessed of adornment", as you say أَجْرَبَ الرَّجُلُ when the man comes to have mangy camels. The yāʾ was kept sound, whereas by analogy it should be changed to alif; but it came sound, just as اسْتَحْوَذَ came.
It is also read «وَازْيَأَنَّتْ», with a light vowelless zāy, after it a yāʾ with fatḥa, after it a hamza, after it a doubled nūn. The origin is وَازْيَانَّتْ, like احْمَارَّتْ, but the alif was given a vowel and so changed into a hamza, as we mentioned at «الضَّالِّينَ».
(تَغْنَ بِالْأَمْسِ): it was read among the irregular (shādhdh) readings «تَتَغَنَّ», with two tāʾs, and it is in the well-known reading. «[Translator's note: so in the text; the clause "and it is in the well-known reading" seems to mean that the sense is the same as that of the well-known reading تَغْنَ.]»
And «الْأَمْس» here means past time, not literally the "yesterday" that is before your day. When it is meant in that sense it is declinable (muʿrab), and it is without the article and without a genitive construct, indefinite.

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا الْحُسْنَى وَزِيَادَةٌ وَلَا يَرْهَقُ وُجُوهَهُمْ قَتَرٌ وَلَا ذِلَّةٌ أُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ الْجَنَّةِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ (٢٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَا يَرْهَقُ وُجُوهَهُمْ): the clause is resumptive.
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), what governs it being the settledness (istiqrār) in «لِلَّذِينَ»; i.e. "the best reward is settled for them, safety being guaranteed to them", and the like. It cannot be conjoined to الْحُسْنَى, because when a verb is conjoined to a maṣdar (verbal noun) it needs «أَنْ», either stated or implied, and «أَنْ» is not implied, because the verb is nominative (indicative).

ukberi-tibyan:27-27.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالَّذِينَ كَسَبُوا السَّيِّئَاتِ جَزَاءُ سَيِّئَةٍ بِمِثْلِهَا وَتَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ مَا لَهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ عَاصِمٍ كَأَنَّمَا أُغْشِيَتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ قِطَعًا مِنَ اللَّيْلِ مُظْلِمًا أُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ (٢٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالَّذِينَ كَسَبُوا): a mubtadaʾ (subject). Regarding the khabar (predicate) there are two views. First: it is His saying «مَا لَهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ عَاصِمٍ», or His saying (كَأَنَّمَا أُغْشِيَتْ), or His saying (أُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ); and (جَزَاءُ سَيِّئَةٍ بِمِثْلِهَا) is then parenthetical between the mubtadaʾ and its khabar. Second: the khabar is (جَزَاءُ سَيِّئَةٍ), and جَزَاءُ is a mubtadaʾ. Regarding its khabar there are two views. First: بِمِثْلِهَا, the bāʾ being redundant (zāʾida), as in His saying (وَجَزَاءُ سَيِّئَةٍ سَيِّئَةٌ مِثْلُهَا); it may also be non-redundant, the implied form being: "the recompense of an evil deed is measured by its like". Second: that the bāʾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to جَزَاءٌ and the khabar is omitted; i.e. "and the recompense of an evil deed with its like takes place".
(وَتَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ): it is said: it is conjoined to كَسَبُوا; but that is weak, because the imperfect is not conjoined to the past; and if it is said that it is in the sense of the past, that is weak too. It is also said: the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). (قِطَعًا): it is read with fatḥa on the ṭāʾ, as the plural of قِطْعَةٌ ("piece"), and it is the second object of «أُغْشِيَتْ».
And (مِنَ اللَّيْلِ) is a naʿt (adjective) of قِطَعٌ.
And (مُظْلِمًا) is a ḥāl from اللَّيْلِ. It is also said: from «قِطَعٍ», or a naʿt of «قِطَعٍ», made masculine because القِطَع has the meaning of "a great amount".
It is also read with sukūn on the ṭāʾ; on this view «مُظْلِمًا» is a naʿt of قِطْعٌ, or a ḥāl from it, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مِنَ اللَّيْلِ», or a ḥāl from «اللَّيْلِ».

ukberi-tibyan:28-28.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَوْمَ نَحْشُرُهُمْ جَمِيعًا ثُمَّ نَقُولُ لِلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا مَكَانَكُمْ أَنْتُمْ وَشُرَكَاؤُكُمْ فَزَيَّلْنَا بَيْنَهُمْ وَقَالَ شُرَكَاؤُهُمْ مَا كُنْتُمْ إِيَّانَا تَعْبُدُونَ (٢٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَكَانَكُمْ): it is an adverb (ẓarf), indeclinable (mabnī) because it occurs in the place of the imperative, i.e. "keep (to your place)!"; and it contains an agent pronoun.
And (أَنْتُمْ) is a tawkīd (emphasis) of it. «The kāf and the mīm» are in the position of the genitive according to some; according to others the kāf is for address and has no position, like the kāf in إِيَّاكُمْ.
(وَشُرَكَاؤُكُمْ) is conjoined to the agent.
(فَزَيَّلْنَا): the middle radical (ʿayn) of the word is wāw, because it is from زَالَ يَزُولُ. It was changed to yāʾ only because the pattern of the word is fayʿal, i.e. زَيْوَلْنَا, like بَيْطَرَ and بَيْقَرَ; when the yāʾ and the wāw came together under the well-known condition, it was changed to yāʾ. It is also said: it is from زِلْتُ الشَّيْءَ أَزِيلُهُ ("I separated the thing"), so that on this view its middle radical is yāʾ, and on this view it may be either faʿʿalnā or fayʿalnā.

ukberi-tibyan:30-30.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هُنَالِكَ تَبْلُو كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَا أَسْلَفَتْ وَرُدُّوا إِلَى اللَّهِ مَوْلَاهُمُ الْحَقِّ وَضَلَّ عَنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ (٣٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هُنَالِكَ تَبْلُو): it is read with yāʾ, i.e. "its deeds are tested". «[Translator's note: so in the text («بِالْيَاءِ»); the reading meant is presumably تَبْلُو with bāʾ («بِالْبَاءِ»), "tests, experiences".]»
And it is read with tāʾ, i.e. "follows", or "reads in the record".

ukberi-tibyan:33-33.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَذَلِكَ حَقَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ فَسَقُوا أَنَّهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ (٣٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنَّهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ): أَنَّ and what it governs are in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) from «كَلِمَةُ»; or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); or in the position of the accusative, i.e. "because they"; or in the position of the genitive, by the lām operating while omitted.

ukberi-tibyan:34-34.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ هَلْ مِنْ شُرَكَائِكُمْ مَنْ يَبْدَأُ الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ قُلِ اللَّهُ يَبْدَأُ الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ فَأَنَّى تُؤْفَكُونَ) (٣٤) (قُلْ هَلْ مِنْ شُرَكَائِكُمْ مَنْ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْحَقِّ قُلِ اللَّهُ يَهْدِي لِلْحَقِّ أَفَمَنْ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْحَقِّ أَحَقُّ أَنْ يُتَّبَعَ أَمَّنْ لَا يَهِدِّي إِلَّا أَنْ يُهْدَى فَمَا لَكُمْ كَيْفَ تَحْكُمُونَ (٣٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَمَّنْ لَا يَهِدِّي): there are readings of it similar to which we have mentioned at His saying (يَخْطَفُ أَبْصَارَهُمْ), and we explained them there.
As for (إِلَّا أَنْ يُهْدَى), it is like His saying (إِلَّا أَنْ يَصَّدَّقُوا), which was mentioned in al-Nisāʾ; and it has parallels that have also been mentioned.
(فَمَا لَكُمْ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); i.e. "what is there for you in associating partners?".
And (كَيْفَ تَحْكُمُونَ): resumptive; i.e. "how do you judge that He has a partner?".

ukberi-tibyan:36-36.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا يَتَّبِعُ أَكْثَرُهُمْ إِلَّا ظَنًّا إِنَّ الظَّنَّ لَا يُغْنِي مِنَ الْحَقِّ شَيْئًا إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ بِمَا يَفْعَلُونَ (١٢)) «[Translator's note: the verse number is printed as (١٢); this is verse 36.]»
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا يُغْنِي مِنَ الْحَقِّ شَيْئًا): it is in the position of the maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "any availing".
It may also be the object of يُغْنِي, with (مِنَ الْحَقِّ) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it.

ukberi-tibyan:37-37.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا كَانَ هَذَا الْقُرْآنُ أَنْ يُفْتَرَى مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ وَلَكِنْ تَصْدِيقَ الَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَتَفْصِيلَ الْكِتَابِ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ (٣٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا كَانَ هَذَا الْقُرْآنُ): (هَذَا) is the ism (subject) of kāna, and (الْقُرْآنُ) is a naʿt (adjective) of it or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). Regarding (أَنْ يُفْتَرَى) there are three views. First: it is the khabar (predicate) of kāna; i.e. "the Qurʾan was not a fabrication", the maṣdar (verbal noun) here being in the sense of the passive participle, i.e. "fabricated". Second: the implied form is "the Qurʾan was not a thing of fabrication". Third: that the khabar of kāna is omitted, the implied form being: "this Qurʾan was not such that it could be fabricated". It is also said: the implied form is "for being fabricated".
And (تَصْدِيقَ) is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); i.e. "but it was sent down for confirmation".
It is also said: the implied form is "but it was the confirmation of that which …", i.e. "confirming that which …".
(وَتَفْصِيلَ الْكِتَابِ): like تَصْدِيقَ.
(لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْكِتَابِ, «الْكِتَابِ» being an object in meaning; and it may be resumptive.
(مِنْ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ): it may be another ḥāl, or it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to the omitted element; i.e. "but it was sent down from the Lord of the worlds".

ukberi-tibyan:39-39.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (بَلْ كَذَّبُوا بِمَا لَمْ يُحِيطُوا بِعِلْمِهِ وَلَمَّا يَأْتِهِمْ تَأْوِيلُهُ كَذَلِكَ كَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الظَّالِمِينَ (٣٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: «كَيْفَ» is the khabar (predicate) of kāna, and «عَاقِبَةُ» is its ism (subject).

ukberi-tibyan:43-43.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَسْتَمِعُونَ إِلَيْكَ أَفَأَنْتَ تُسْمِعُ الصُّمَّ وَلَوْ كَانُوا لَا يَعْقِلُونَ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَنْظُرُ إِلَيْكَ أَفَأَنْتَ تَهْدِي الْعُمْيَ وَلَوْ كَانُوا لَا يُبْصِرُونَ (٤٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَنْ يَسْتَمِعُونَ إِلَيْكَ): the plural is according to the meaning of (مَنْ), and the singular in His saying, Exalted is He, (مَنْ يَنْظُرُ) is according to its wording.

ukberi-tibyan:44-44.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَظْلِمُ النَّاسَ شَيْئًا وَلَكِنَّ النَّاسَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ (٤٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا يَظْلِمُ النَّاسَ شَيْئًا): it may be an object, i.e. "He does not diminish them anything"; or it may be in the position of the maṣdar (verbal noun).

ukberi-tibyan:45-45.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَوْمَ يَحْشُرُهُمْ كَأَنْ لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا إِلَّا سَاعَةً مِنَ النَّهَارِ يَتَعَارَفُونَ بَيْنَهُمْ قَدْ خَسِرَ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِلِقَاءِ اللَّهِ وَمَا كَانُوا مُهْتَدِينَ (٤٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَأَنْ لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا): the whole phrase is in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial), and what governs it is (يَحْشُرُهُمْ). كَأَنْ here is lightened from the heavy (form), and its ism (noun) is omitted, i.e. "as though they".
And (سَاعَةً) is an adverb (ẓarf) for يَلْبَثُوا, and (مِنَ النَّهَارِ) is a naʿt (adjective) of سَاعَةً. It is also said: «كَأَنْ لَمْ» is a naʿt of the day (al-yawm), the referring pronoun being omitted, i.e. "they had not tarried before it". It is also said: it is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a gathering as though they had not tarried before it"; and what governs «يَوْمَ» is "remember (udhkur)".
(يَتَعَارَفُونَ) is another ḥāl, governed by «يَحْشُرُهُمْ»; and it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because the mutual recognition does not happen at the time of the gathering.
(قَدْ خَسِرَ): it may be resumptive; and the implied form may be: "saying: قَدْ خَسِرَ", the omitted element being a ḥāl from the pronoun in يَتَعَارَفُونَ.

ukberi-tibyan:46-46.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِمَّا نُرِيَنَّكَ بَعْضَ الَّذِي نَعِدُهُمْ أَوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ فَإِلَيْنَا مَرْجِعُهُمْ ثُمَّ اللَّهُ شَهِيدٌ عَلَى مَا يَفْعَلُونَ (٤٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ثُمَّ اللَّهُ شَهِيدٌ): ثُمَّ here does not entail sequence in meaning; it only arranges the statements one after another, as when you say: زَيْدٌ عَالِمٌ، ثُمَّ هُوَ كَرِيمٌ ("Zayd is learned, and then he is generous").

ukberi-tibyan:50-50.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَتَاكُمْ عَذَابُهُ بَيَاتًا أَوْ نَهَارًا مَاذَا يَسْتَعْجِلُ مِنْهُ الْمُجْرِمُونَ (٥٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَاذَا يَسْتَعْجِلُ): we have mentioned two views on (مَاذَا) in al-Baqara at His saying, Exalted is He, (مَاذَا يُنْفِقُونَ), and both are held here. It is also said that there is a third view on it: that «مَاذَا» is a single noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «يَسْتَعْجِلُ مِنْهُ» is the khabar (predicate). This has been judged weak on the grounds that the khabar here is a clause consisting of a verb and its agent with no pronoun in it referring back to the mubtadaʾ. This objection was rejected on the grounds that the referring pronoun is the hāʾ in «مِنْهُ», so it is like your saying: زَيْدٌ أَخَذْتُ مِنْهُ دِرْهَمًا ("Zayd — I took a dirham from him").

ukberi-tibyan:51-51.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَثُمَّ إِذَا مَا وَقَعَ آمَنْتُمْ بِهِ آلْآنَ وَقَدْ كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ (٥١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (آلْآنَ): there is a discussion about it, the like of which was mentioned in al-Baqara. What puts it in the accusative is omitted, its implied form being: "do you believe now?".

ukberi-tibyan:53-53.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَسْتَنْبِئُونَكَ أَحَقٌّ هُوَ قُلْ إِي وَرَبِّي إِنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ وَمَا أَنْتُمْ بِمُعْجِزِينَ (٥٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَحَقٌّ هُوَ): a mubtadaʾ (subject). It is also possible that «هُوَ» is the mubtadaʾ and «أَحَقٌّ» the khabar (predicate). The position of the clause is accusative, by «يَسْتَنْبِئُونَكَ».
And (إِي) is in the sense of نَعَمْ ("yes").

ukberi-tibyan:54-54.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَوْ أَنَّ لِكُلِّ نَفْسٍ ظَلَمَتْ مَا فِي الْأَرْضِ لَافْتَدَتْ بِهِ وَأَسَرُّوا النَّدَامَةَ لَمَّا رَأَوُا الْعَذَابَ وَقُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ بِالْقِسْطِ وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ (٥٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَسَرُّوا النَّدَامَةَ): resumptive; it is a narration of what will happen in the Hereafter. It is also said: it is in the sense of the future. It is also said: that took place in this world.

ukberi-tibyan:57-57.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ قَدْ جَاءَتْكُمْ مَوْعِظَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَشِفَاءٌ لِمَا فِي الصُّدُورِ وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةٌ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ (٥٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَشِفَاءٌ): it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of the active participle, i.e. "and a healer". It is also said: it is in the sense of the passive participle, i.e. "that by which healing is obtained".

ukberi-tibyan:58-58.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ بِفَضْلِ اللَّهِ وَبِرَحْمَتِهِ فَبِذَلِكَ فَلْيَفْرَحُوا هُوَ خَيْرٌ مِمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ (٥٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَبِذَلِكَ فَلْيَفْرَحُوا): the first fāʾ is linked to what precedes it, and the second to an omitted verb, its implied form being: "so let them marvel at that, and let them rejoice", as in their saying زَيْدًا فَاضْرِبْهُ, i.e. "aim at Zayd, and strike him". It is also said: the first fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida).
The majority read it with yāʾ, and it is a command to the absent third person; it is a turn from address to the third person.
It is also read with tāʾ, as address, like what precedes it.

ukberi-tibyan:59-59.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ مِنْ رِزْقٍ فَجَعَلْتُمْ مِنْهُ حَرَامًا وَحَلَالًا قُلْ آللَّهُ أَذِنَ لَكُمْ أَمْ عَلَى اللَّهِ تَفْتَرُونَ (٥٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَرَأَيْتُمْ): it has been mentioned in al-Anʿām.
(آللَّهُ) is like (آلذَّكَرَيْنِ), and it has been mentioned in al-Anʿām.

ukberi-tibyan:61-61.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا تَكُونُ فِي شَأْنٍ وَمَا تَتْلُو مِنْهُ مِنْ قُرْآنٍ وَلَا تَعْمَلُونَ مِنْ عَمَلٍ إِلَّا كُنَّا عَلَيْكُمْ شُهُودًا إِذْ تُفِيضُونَ فِيهِ وَمَا يَعْزُبُ عَنْ رَبِّكَ مِنْ مِثْقَالِ ذَرَّةٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ وَلَا أَصْغَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ وَلَا أَكْبَرَ إِلَّا فِي كِتَابٍ مُبِينٍ (٦١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي شَأْنٍ): the khabar (predicate) of kāna.
(وَمَا تَتْلُو): مَا is negating; and (مِنْهُ), i.e. "from the matter (al-shaʾn)", i.e. "on account of it"; and (مِنْ قُرْآنٍ) is the object of تَتْلُو, with مِنْ redundant (zāʾida).
(إِلَّا كُنَّا عَلَيْكُمْ شُهُودًا إِذْ تُفِيضُونَ): an adverb (ẓarf) for «شُهُودًا».
(مِنْ مِثْقَالِ): in the position of the nominative by يَعْزُبُ. And يَعْزُبُ, with ḍamma on the zāy and with kasra, are two dialectal forms, and it has been read with both.
(وَلَا أَصْغَرَ) (وَلَا أَكْبَرَ), with fatḥa on the rāʾ: in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of «ذَرَّةٍ» or of «مِثْقَالِ», according to the wording. Both are also read in the nominative, construed with the position of «مِنْ مِثْقَالِ». The one in Sabaʾ will be mentioned in its place, if Allah the Exalted wills.
(إِلَّا فِي كِتَابٍ): i.e. "except that it is in a Book"; and the exception is disjoined (munqaṭiʿ).

ukberi-tibyan:64-64.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَكَانُوا يَتَّقُونَ لَهُمُ الْبُشْرَى فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ لَا تَبْدِيلَ لِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ ذَلِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ (٦٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): it may be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with its khabar (predicate) «لَهُمُ الْبُشْرَى». It may be a second khabar of inna, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are those who …". It may be accusative by implying أَعْنِي ("I mean"), or a naʿt (adjective) of أَوْلِيَاءَ after the khabar. It is also said: it may be in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) from the hāʾ and mīm in «عَلَيْهِمْ».
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا): «فِي» may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to الْبُشْرَى, or be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it, what governs it being the settledness (istiqrār).
And (لَا تَبْدِيلَ): resumptive.

ukberi-tibyan:65-65.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا يَحْزُنْكَ قَوْلُهُمْ إِنَّ الْعِزَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ (٦٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنَّ الْعِزَّةَ): it is resumptive, and the pause is on what precedes it.

ukberi-tibyan:66-66.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَا إِنَّ لِلَّهِ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَمَا يَتَّبِعُ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ شُرَكَاءَ إِنْ يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ وَإِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا يَخْرُصُونَ (٦٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا يَتَّبِعُ): there are two views on it. First: it is negating, and the object of «يَتَّبِعُ» is omitted, indicated by His saying «إِنْ يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ».
And «شُرَكَاءَ» is the object of «يَدْعُونَ»; it cannot be the object of «يَتَّبِعُونَ», because the meaning would then become that they did not follow partners, and that is not the case. The second view: that (مَا) is interrogative, in the position of the accusative by «يَتَّبِعُ».

ukberi-tibyan:68-68.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالُوا اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ وَلَدًا سُبْحَانَهُ هُوَ الْغَنِيُّ لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ إِنْ عِنْدَكُمْ مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ بِهَذَا أَتَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ (٦٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنْ عِنْدَكُمْ مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ): إِنْ here is in the sense of «مَا» ("not") and nothing else.
(بِهَذَا): attached (mutaʿalliq) to سُلْطَانٍ, or a naʿt (adjective) of it.

ukberi-tibyan:70-70.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَتَاعٌ فِي الدُّنْيَا ثُمَّ إِلَيْنَا مَرْجِعُهُمْ ثُمَّ نُذِيقُهُمُ الْعَذَابَ الشَّدِيدَ بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْفُرُونَ (٧٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَتَاعٌ فِي الدُّنْيَا): the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: "their fabrication", or "their life", or "their going about", and the like.

ukberi-tibyan:71-71.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ نُوحٍ إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِ يَا قَوْمِ إِنْ كَانَ كَبُرَ عَلَيْكُمْ مَقَامِي وَتَذْكِيرِي بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ فَعَلَى اللَّهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ فَأَجْمِعُوا أَمْرَكُمْ وَشُرَكَاءَكُمْ ثُمَّ لَا يَكُنْ أَمْرُكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ غُمَّةً ثُمَّ اقْضُوا إِلَيَّ وَلَا تُنْظِرُونِ (٧١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِ): «إِذْ» is an adverb (ẓarf), and what governs it is «نَبَأُ»; it may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(فَعَلَى اللَّهِ): the fāʾ is that of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). The fāʾ in «فَأَجْمِعُوا» conjoins to the apodosis. «وَأَجْمِعُوا» is with the disjunctive hamza (hamzat al-qaṭʿ), from your saying أَجْمَعْتُ عَلَى الْأَمْرِ, when you have resolved upon it; except that the preposition was omitted, so the verb reached it by itself.
It is also said: it is originally transitive by itself; and of this is the saying of al-Ḥārith:
أَجْمَعُوا أَمْرَهُمْ بِلَيْلٍ فَلَمَّا ... أَصْبَحُوا أَصْبَحَتْ لَهُمْ ضَوْضَاءُ
("They resolved upon their affair by night; and when they rose in the morning, a clamour arose among them.")
As for (شُرَكَاءَكُمْ), the majority read it in the accusative, and there are several views on it. First: it is conjoined to «أَمْرَكُمْ», its implied form being "and the affair of your partners", the muḍāf ilayhi being put in the place of the muḍāf. Second: it is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), its implied form being "together with your partners". Third: it is accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "and gather your partners". It is also said: the implied form is "and call your partners".
It is also read in the nominative, conjoined to the pronoun in «أَجْمِعُوا».
It is also read «فَاجْمَعُوا», with the connective hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) and fatḥa on the mīm; the implied form is then "those concerned in your affair", because you say جَمَعْتُ الْقَوْمَ ("I gathered the people") and أَجْمَعْتُ الْأَمْرَ ("I resolved upon the affair"), but you do not say جَمَعْتُ الْأَمْرَ in this sense. It is also said: there is no omission in it, because what is meant by "gathering" here is joining some of their affairs to others.
(ثُمَّ اقْضُوا إِلَيَّ): it is read with qāf and ḍād, from قَضَيْتُ الْأَمْرَ ("I carried out the matter"); the meaning is: "carry out what you have resolved upon of falling upon me".
It is also read with fatḥa on the hamza, with fāʾ and ḍād; its maṣdar (verbal noun) is الْإِفْضَاءُ, and the meaning is "reach me". The final radical (lām) of the word is wāw; one says فَضَا الْمَكَانُ يَفْضُو, when the place becomes wide.

ukberi-tibyan:74-74.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ بَعَثْنَا مِنْ بَعْدِهِ رُسُلًا إِلَى قَوْمِهِمْ فَجَاءُوهُمْ بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ فَمَا كَانُوا لِيُؤْمِنُوا بِمَا كَذَّبُوا بِهِ مِنْ قَبْلُ كَذَلِكَ نَطْبَعُ عَلَى قُلُوبِ الْمُعْتَدِينَ (٧٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ بَعْدِهِ): the hāʾ refers to Nūḥ, upon him be peace.
(فَمَا كَانُوا): the wāw is the pronoun of the peoples, the pronoun in (كَذَّبُوا) refers to the people of Nūḥ, and the hāʾ in (بِهِ) is for Nūḥ. The meaning is: "the peoples of the messengers who came after Nūḥ would not believe in that which the people of Nūḥ had denied", i.e. in its like.
It is also possible that the hāʾ is for Nūḥ with no omission in it, the meaning being: "the peoples of the messengers who came after Nūḥ would not believe in Nūḥ, upon him be peace". «[Translator's note: so in the text; the hāʾ is assigned to Nūḥ in both views, although the paraphrase of the first view ("in that which … i.e. in its like") treats it as referring to «مَا».]»

ukberi-tibyan:77-77.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ مُوسَى أَتَقُولُونَ لِلْحَقِّ لَمَّا جَاءَكُمْ أَسِحْرٌ هَذَا وَلَا يُفْلِحُ السَّاحِرُونَ (٧٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَتَقُولُونَ لِلْحَقِّ لَمَّا جَاءَكُمْ): what is reported by يَقُولُ is omitted; i.e. "do you say of it: it is sorcery!". Then he began anew and said: «أَسِحْرٌ هَذَا»? And «سِحْرٌ» is a fronted khabar (predicate), and هَذَا is the mubtadaʾ (subject).

ukberi-tibyan:78-78.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالُوا أَجِئْتَنَا لِتَلْفِتَنَا عَمَّا وَجَدْنَا عَلَيْهِ آبَاءَنَا وَتَكُونَ لَكُمَا الْكِبْرِيَاءُ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَمَا نَحْنُ لَكُمَا بِمُؤْمِنِينَ (٧٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الْكِبْرِيَاءُ فِي الْأَرْضِ): it is the ism (subject) of kāna, and «لَكُمْ» is its khabar (predicate). «[Translator's note: so printed; the āya has لَكُمَا.]» And «فِي الْأَرْضِ» is an adverb (ẓarf) for الْكِبْرِيَاءُ, made accusative by it, or by كَانَ, or by the settledness (istiqrār) in «لَكُمَا». It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْكِبْرِيَاءُ, or from the pronoun in «لَكُمَا».

ukberi-tibyan:81-81.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَمَّا أَلْقَوْا قَالَ مُوسَى مَا جِئْتُمْ بِهِ السِّحْرُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَيُبْطِلُهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُصْلِحُ عَمَلَ الْمُفْسِدِينَ (٨١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا جِئْتُمْ بِهِ السِّحْرُ): it is read as a question; on this view (مَا) is interrogative, and regarding its position there are two views. First: it is accusative by an omitted verb whose place is after (مَا), its implied form being "what thing have you brought?", «جِئْتُمْ بِهِ» explaining the omitted verb.
On this view there are two possibilities regarding His saying (السِّحْرُ). First: it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is sorcery?". Second: that the khabar is omitted, i.e. "is it sorcery (al-siḥru huwa)?".
Second: its position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with «جِئْتُمْ بِهِ» as the khabar.
And regarding (السِّحْرُ) there are then two possibilities. First: the two views already given. Second: it is a badal (substitute) from the position of (مَا), as you say: مَا عِنْدَكَ أَدِينَارٌ أَمْ دِرْهَمٌ؟ ("What do you have — a dinar or a dirham?").
It is also read in the form of a statement, and there are two views on it. First: it too is a question in meaning, the hamza having been omitted because it is understood. Second: it is a statement in meaning; on this view (مَا) is in the sense of الَّذِي ("that which"), «جِئْتُمْ بِهِ» is its ṣila (relative clause), and «السِّحْرُ» its khabar.
It is also possible that (مَا) is interrogative and (السِّحْرُ) the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ.

ukberi-tibyan:83-83.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَمَا آمَنَ لِمُوسَى إِلَّا ذُرِّيَّةٌ مِنْ قَوْمِهِ عَلَى خَوْفٍ مِنْ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَئِهِمْ أَنْ يَفْتِنَهُمْ وَإِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ لَعَالٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَإِنَّهُ لَمِنَ الْمُسْرِفِينَ (٨٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَلَئِهِمْ): regarding what the hāʾ and mīm refer to there are several views. First: it refers to the offspring (al-dhurriyya); it is not feminine because the dhurriyya are a people, so it is masculine in meaning. Second: it refers to the people (al-qawm). Third: it refers to Firʿawn; and it is plural for two reasons. First: since Firʿawn was great in their eyes, the pronoun referred to him in the plural form, just as a great man says: "We command". Second: Firʿawn became a name for his followers, just as Thamūd is a name for the whole tribe. It is also said: the pronoun refers to something omitted, its implied form being "from the family (āl) of Firʿawn and their chiefs", i.e. the chiefs of the family. In our view this is an error, because a pronoun does not refer to what is omitted; if that were permissible, you could say زَيْدٌ قَامُوا ("Zayd — they stood") meaning "Zayd's servants stood".
(أَنْ يَفْتِنَهُمْ): it is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) from فِرْعَوْنَ; its implied form is: "in fear of a trial from Firʿawn".
It may also be in the position of the accusative by خَوْفٍ; i.e. "in fear of Firʿawn's trying them".

ukberi-tibyan:87-87.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى مُوسَى وَأَخِيهِ أَنْ تَبَوَّءَا لِقَوْمِكُمَا بِمِصْرَ بُيُوتًا وَاجْعَلُوا بُيُوتَكُمْ قِبْلَةً وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَبَشِّرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (٨٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ تَبَوَّآ): (أَنْ) may be the explicative أَنْ, having no grammatical position; or it may be maṣdariyya (forming a maṣdar), in which case it is in the position of the accusative by أَوْحَيْنَا.
The majority pronounce the hamza fully (taḥqīq); some of them made it a yāʾ, the yāʾ replacing the hamza for lightening.
(لِقَوْمِكُمَا): there are two views on it. First: the lām is not redundant, and the implied form is "take houses for your people"; on this view لِقَوْمِكُمَا may be one of the two objects of تَبَوَّءَا, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْبُيُوتَ. Second: the lām is redundant (zāʾida), and the implied form is "settle your people in houses", i.e. "lodge them"; tafaʿʿala and faʿʿala have one meaning, like عَلَّقَهَا and تَعَلَّقَهَا.
As for His saying «بِمِصْرَ», it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to تَبَوَّءَا, or be a ḥāl from الْبُيُوتَ, or a ḥāl from قَوْمِكُمَا, or a ḥāl from the agent pronoun in تَبَوَّأَ — and in this last there is weakness.
(وَاجْعَلُوا) — (وَأَقِيمُوا): He used the plural in both only because He meant Mūsā and Hārūn, Allah's blessings be upon them both, together with their people; and He used the singular in His saying «وَبَشِّرْ» because He meant Mūsā, upon him be peace, alone, since he was the Messenger and Hārūn was a minister (wazīr) to him; so Mūsā, upon him be peace, is the principal.

ukberi-tibyan:88-88.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ مُوسَى رَبَّنَا إِنَّكَ آتَيْتَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَأَهُ زِينَةً وَأَمْوَالًا فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا رَبَّنَا لِيُضِلُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِكَ رَبَّنَا اطْمِسْ عَلَى أَمْوَالِهِمْ وَاشْدُدْ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ فَلَا يُؤْمِنُوا حَتَّى يَرَوُا الْعَذَابَ الْأَلِيمَ (٨٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَلَا يُؤْمِنُوا): regarding its position there are two views. First: the accusative; and in this there are two possibilities. First: it is conjoined to «لِيَضِلُّوا». Second: it is the answer to the supplication in His saying اطْمِسْ and اشْدُدْ. The second view: its position is jussive (majzūm), because its meaning is supplication, as you say: لَا تُعَذِّبْنِي ("do not punish me").

ukberi-tibyan:89-89.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ قَدْ أُجِيبَتْ دَعْوَتُكُمَا فَاسْتَقِيمَا وَلَا تَتَّبِعَانِّ سَبِيلَ الَّذِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ (٨٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَا تَتَّبِعَانِّ): it is read with a doubled nūn; the nūn is for emphasis, and the verb is indeclinable (mabnī) with it. The nūn that enters as the sign of the indicative has no place here, because the verb here is not declinable.
It is also read with a light nūn with kasra, and there are two views on it.
First: it is also a prohibition, and the first nūn of the heavy (nūn) was omitted for lightening; the second was not omitted, because had it been omitted a vowelled nūn would have been omitted and the vowelless one would have needed to be given a vowel, while omitting the vowelless one is less of a change. The second view: the verb is declinable (muʿrab) and indicative (marfūʿ); and there are two possibilities in this. First: it is a statement with the meaning of prohibition, as we mentioned at His saying (لَا تَعْبُدُونَ إِلَّا اللَّهَ). Second: it is in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial), the implied form being "so go straight, not following".

ukberi-tibyan:90-90.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَجَاوَزْنَا بِبَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ الْبَحْرَ فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ فِرْعَوْنُ وَجُنُودُهُ بَغْيًا وَعَدْوًا حَتَّى إِذَا أَدْرَكَهُ الْغَرَقُ قَالَ آمَنْتُ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا الَّذِي آمَنَتْ بِهِ بَنُو إِسْرَائِيلَ وَأَنَا مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ (٩٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَجَاوَزْنَا بِبَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ): the bāʾ is for making transitive (taʿdiya), like the hamza, as you say: أَجَزْتُ الرِّجَالَ الْبَحْرَ ("I brought the men across the sea").
(بَغْيًا وَعَدْوًا): a mafʿūl min ajlihi (object of purpose), or a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:91-91.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (آلْآنَ وَقَدْ عَصَيْتَ قَبْلُ وَكُنْتَ مِنَ الْمُفْسِدِينَ (٩١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (آلْآنَ): what governs it is omitted, its implied form being: "do you believe now?".

ukberi-tibyan:92-92.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَالْيَوْمَ نُنَجِّيكَ بِبَدَنِكَ لِتَكُونَ لِمَنْ خَلْفَكَ آيَةً وَإِنَّ كَثِيرًا مِنَ النَّاسِ عَنْ آيَاتِنَا لَغَافِلُونَ (٩٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِبَدَنِكَ): in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial); i.e. "naked".
It is also said: "with your body, with no soul in it". It is also said: "with your coat of mail".

ukberi-tibyan:93-93.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ بَوَّأْنَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ مُبَوَّأَ صِدْقٍ وَرَزَقْنَاهُمْ مِنَ الطَّيِّبَاتِ فَمَا اخْتَلَفُوا حَتَّى جَاءَهُمُ الْعِلْمُ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَقْضِي بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ فِيمَا كَانُوا فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ (٩٢)). «[Translator's note: the verse number is printed as (٩٢); this is verse 93.]»
His saying, Exalted is He: (مُبَوَّأَ صِدْقٍ): it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun), or it may be a place.

ukberi-tibyan:98-98.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَوْلَا كَانَتْ قَرْيَةٌ آمَنَتْ فَنَفَعَهَا إِيمَانُهَا إِلَّا قَوْمَ يُونُسَ لَمَّا آمَنُوا كَشَفْنَا عَنْهُمْ عَذَابَ الْخِزْيِ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَمَتَّعْنَاهُمْ إِلَى حِينٍ (٩٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا قَوْمَ يُونُسَ): it is accusative as a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because what is excepted from is the town, and it is not of the same kind as the people. It is also said: it is a joined exception (muttaṣil), because the implied form is "why was there not the people of a town". Had it been read in the nominative, إِلَّا in it would have been in the position of «غَيْرُ», and so it would be a naʿt (adjective).

ukberi-tibyan:101-101.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلِ انْظُرُوا مَاذَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا تُغْنِي الْآيَاتُ وَالنُّذُرُ عَنْ قَوْمٍ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ (١٠١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَاذَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ): it is an interrogative in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); «فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ» is the khabar (predicate), and «انْظُرُوا» is suspended (muʿallaqa) from governing.
It may also be in the sense of الَّذِي ("that which"); the basis of this has preceded.
(وَمَا تُغْنِي): it may be interrogative, in the position of the accusative, or it may be negation.

ukberi-tibyan:103-103.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ نُنَجِّي رُسُلَنَا وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كَذَلِكَ حَقًّا عَلَيْنَا نُنْجِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (١٠٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَذَلِكَ حَقًّا): there are three views on it.
First: that «كَذَلِكَ» is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a rescuing like that", and حَقًّا is a badal (substitute) from it. Second: that both are accusative by the «نُنْجِ» that comes after them. Third: that «كَذَلِكَ» belongs to the first and حَقًّا to the second.
It is also possible that «كَذَلِكَ» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "the matter is like that", with «حَقًّا» accusative by what comes after it. Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَنْ أَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفًا وَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ (١٠٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَنْ أَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ): the like of it has been mentioned in al-Anʿām.
